texts.facts: Aggrieved by the adjudication of the Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate instant appeals have been preferred, assailing the impugned order dated 11.01.2023 whereby the appellants were found to have violated the provisions of Section 26 (2) (ii) of Food Safety and Standard Act 2006 (the Act hereinafter) read with Section 3 (1) (zx) of the said Act which is punishable under Section 51 of the Act. Those samples were further subjected to analysis and examination by the Food Safety Officer from NABL accredited FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.2 of 9 laboratory, where on examination it was found that sample was sub-standard since total ash on dry basis exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 7.0% by weight. The Designated Officer was provided with the case file including the Food Analyst's report and Food Safety Officer's report, and after obtaining the sanction for prosecution under Section 36 (3) (e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, an application was moved before the Adjudicating Officer for summoning, trial and punishment to the accused persons which ultimately resulted into the impugned order.
texts.arguments: In such circumstances, merely having address Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/ 2 on the label cannot be enough to link and connect the appellant Krishan Masala Company and its partners with the adulterated Dhaniya Powder. There is no investigation on this aspect and therefore, when the shop owner, who has failed to produce any document, which may have even remotely indicated that the "Dhaniya Powder" in question was supplied by Krishna Masala Company, then in these circumstances, the appellant Krishna Masala Company and its partners cannot be held responsible in any manner so far as, the instant matter is concerned. 6. On the other hand, Ld. counsel for appellant Raj Kumar Sharma has sought to take advantage of Section 80 of the Act but in the absence of any document, which may connect the FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.4 of 9 product in question to the Appellant Krishna Masala Company, the arguments remain bald assertions, having no substance and therefore, appellant Raj Kumar Sharma cannot get any advantage.
